title: He guides the heart
hookLine: no calamity strikes except by Allah's leave, and whoever believes, He guides his heart (64:11)
carry: he guides the heart through it

lines: WORDS FOR WHEN A LOSS STRIKES.
cards: Medina, a small house. A woman named Umm Salama has just lost her husband, Abu Salama, and the grief is still new. She remembers something the Prophet ﷺ taught: words to say when a loss strikes.
She starts to say them, then stops, thinking: who could be better than Abu Salama? She says them anyway. Hold that moment.
Today's verse is about what happens inside a heart right there.

teach.b: Surah At-Taghabun, verse eleven. Pickthall: "No calamity befalleth save by Allah's leave. And whosoever believeth in Allah, He guideth his heart."
The word for calamity is musiba, anything that strikes, from a root meaning to hit the mark. The verse makes two claims. First, nothing happens outside God's permission.
Second, the tender part: for the one who believes, God guides the heart. Not removes the calamity.
Guides the heart through it. A student of the companions named 'Alqama explained it simply: it's the person struck by a loss who knows it is from God, and so accepts it and is content.
Guidance here isn't an answer to why. It's a steadiness in the middle of the not-knowing. Back to Umm Salama.

teach.h: WE ARE GOD'S, AND TO HIM WE RETURN.
teach.b: Muslim records the words the Prophet had taught: we belong to God and to him we return; O God, reward me in my calamity and give me something better in its place. The first half is from Surah Al-Baqarah.
Pickthall: "Lo! we are Allah's and lo! unto Him we are returning."

Umm Salama said it, doubting. Later, the Prophet himself asked to marry her, and she became one of the mothers of the believers. She'd say afterward that God had given her better than Abu Salama: the Messenger of God.
The verse doesn't promise every story turns out like hers. It promises something smaller and closer: a guided heart, steadied in the loss, before anything else changes.

how: When news of a loss comes, Muslims widely say 'inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un', we belong to God and to him we return, and many add the supplication the Prophet taught Umm Salama.

o: the soul's greed, which grips what it has
the mind, which reasons its way to God
the heart, which God guides through loss

games.q: a guided heart — tap the pairs.
p: knows it's from God, and accepts
we are God's, and to him we return

s: the verse promises that the calamity will be removed
it says God guides the believer's heart; the heart is steadied through it.
Umm Salama said the words the Prophet taught even while doubting
she wondered who could be better than Abu Salama, and said them anyway.
'we are God's and to him we return' comes from Surah Al-Baqarah
2:156, said by those who are patient when a calamity strikes.

games.q: you're Umm Salama. your husband has died, and you remember the words to say. you think: who could be better than him? what do you do?
o: stay silent; the words feel untrue.
wait until the grief has passed.
games.why: she said them anyway, and later married the Prophet. she said God had given her better than Abu Salama.

practice: Bring to mind one recent setback, not the biggest grief, something smaller: a plan that fell through, a no, a loss of time or money, and let yourself feel it honestly.
Then, if you pray, say the words Umm Salama said: we belong to God, and to him we return. If not, breathe out slowly and let your shoulders drop, accepting that it happened.

wordCard.voice: Qalb: the heart, which Surah At-Taghabun says God guides, steadying it through loss, for whoever believes. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: he guides his heart. qalb is the heart; the verb is from h-d-y, guidance.

carryVoice: Your line: he guides the heart through it. The week ran from say it, do it, through the Friday prayer, to propped-up timber and Umm Salama's words. Seven more days, done.

sources.q: No calamity befalleth save by Allah's leave. And whosoever believeth in Allah, He guideth his heart.
Lo! we are Allah's and lo! unto Him we are returning.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Tafsir, Surah At-Taghabun ('Alqama's explanation)
